title: The same gate evidence was refused as stale and then reused five minutes later
description:
Observed in the Phase 3 run (epic-9pd, tick cwa, attempt 8), 2026-09-16, and reproduced by computing the digests.

The operator changed .tick/runners.toml's gate command mid-run (bare 'go test -short -count=1 ./...' to the same command with -timeout 45m -parallel 12). Confirmed digests: bare = sha256:a69f0f2e…, flagged = sha256:109e7129….

08:29-08:37  the gate RAN the bare command; evidence gate-cwa-8-go.json records
             check.command = [sh -c go test -short -count=1 ./...] and
             provenance.context_manifest_digest = a69f0.
08:37:09     the run REFUSED to publish it: 'stale_evidence: … a69f0 was gated,
             109e7 is the target now'. Correct — the declared gate had changed.
08:41-08:42  the run was resumed. It adopted attempt 8, saw the work already
             merged, and reported gate_passed on 12472988d0b1 forty seconds
             later — far too fast to have re-run the suite. No new evidence file
             was written: gate-cwa-8-go.json still carries the 08:29-08:37
             timestamps, the bare command and a69f0.
08:42:35     cwa closed 'behind the integrated gate'.

So the tick closed on evidence produced by a command that is no longer the
declared gate, and the identical record was stale on one path and acceptable on
another. One of the two answers is wrong, and the dangerous one is the second:
the whole point of keying evidence by a manifest digest is that a verdict from a
different check is not a verdict about this gate.

Find which path skipped the staleness check — the resume/adopt path that reports
gate_passed for an already-merged attempt looks likeliest, since it did not
re-run anything — and make both paths ask the same question. If reuse is
intended when the source fingerprint is unchanged, then the digest must be part
of that judgement or the digest is decorative.

Not an argument against the doctrine: the 08:37 refusal is the doctrine working.
This is about it being applied unevenly.

acceptance_criteria: Evidence whose context_manifest_digest does not match the current declared gate is refused on EVERY path that can close a tick, including the resume path for an already-merged attempt; a test changes the gate command between gating and closing and asserts the tick is not closed on the old evidence
